depends_on: tensordem.ice_abrasion (DEM contact ensemble, Archard wear, band grid, reference voyage)
tensordem.ice_abrasion_field (N04 interface: panel mesh, profile, P95 connector)

C1_profile_fit.statement: deterministic activity profile fitted to the DEM ensemble-mean rate field
C1_profile_fit.notes: the R^2 on the raw 0.25 m DEM grid is reported separately and is not the criterion; the profile is a panel-scale deterministic model

C2_conditional_simulation.statement: residual random field conditional simulation reproduces its target statistics
metrics: noiseless interpolation error < 1e-6 of the prior std
ensemble variance error < 5 % at m = 100 and m = 400
ensemble mean unbiased within 2 sampling sigma, and < 5 % of the prior std at m = 400

C3_volume_ledger.metric: relative error between the depth field and the rate-model integral

C4_p95_vs_n02.statement: P95 extracted from the evolved field vs the predecessor single-point P95 statistic
C4_p95_vs_n02.metric: relative error (area weighted, one reference voyage)

C5_uniform_anchor.statement: uniform ice field gives d(t) = a t on every panel, with and without moving-frame offsets

C6_performance.statement: >= 1000 panels x 100 time steps evolution plus ledger plus conditional simulation
C6_performance.metric: CPU wall time on one core

known_risks: C4 has a small margin (measured ~9.6 % against a 10 % target) because the smooth profile under-represents pit-scale peaks; it is not tuned.
The DEM ensemble shows no smooth residual above one 0.244 m cell, so the smooth residual covariance comes from documented activity-parameter bands (modelling assumption declared in the report).
The absolute wear level inherits the single-point literature anchor of tensordem.ice_abrasion; nothing new is calibrated.
no_reuse_of_verified_cases: The N04 module (ice_abrasion_field) is not re-verified here; its self-referential checks are replaced by DEM-driven ones. New module, new driver, new figures.
